end.summary:
Practised expanding base-10 numbers using place value and powers of 10, including zero as a placeholder; some examples were right, but the method was not steady yet.
Neel repeatedly treated zero as removable, saying 5,030 and 530 or 305 and 35 could be the same; this was not corrected by the last time it appeared (correctAfterLastSeen: 0).
They identified that 4,075 can be written as 4 × 10³ + 0 × 10² + 7 × 10¹ + 5 × 10⁰.
Next time, check reading each digit’s place and keeping zero placeholders in numbers such as 305, 4,075, and 80,000.
end.parentNote: Asha practised place value, expanded notation with powers of 10, and the role of zero as a placeholder with Neel. Neel correctly set up the expanded form of 4,075, but the mix-up that zero can be dropped was still present at the end and was not corrected later in the lesson. At home, ask them to build numbers with digit cards and say the value of every place, including a zero place, before writing the expanded form.
